question: In November 2025, Narendra Modi presented a revolutionary indigenous innovation of India, as the country’s indigenous quantum security chip called:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Quantum Security Integrated Processor (QSIP)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **November 2025**, Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** unveiled the **Quantum Security Integrated Processor (QSIP)**, marking a historic achievement in India's **indigenous** technological capabilities.
 
• The **QSIP** is India's first fully **locally designed and developed** quantum-secure semiconductor chip, aimed at protecting the nation's **digital sovereignty**.
 
• This innovation is a cornerstone of the **National Quantum Mission (NQM)**, which was initiated to position India as a global leader in **Quantum Technology (QT)**.
 
• The chip is specifically engineered to provide **hardware-level encryption** that is resistant to the immense processing power of future **quantum computers**, which threaten to break existing **RSA** and **ECC** encryption standards.
 
• The development of **QSIP** aligns with the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** initiative, reducing India's reliance on foreign-made **cryptographic modules** and ensuring secure communication for **defense** and **government** sectors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Quantum Mission (NQM):**
 
 
• The **Union Cabinet** approved the **NQM** in **April 2023** with a total financial outlay of **₹6,003.65 crore** for the period **2023-24 to 2030-31**.
 
• The mission aims to develop intermediate-scale **quantum computers** with **50-1000 physical qubits** in various platforms like superconducting and photonic technology.
 
• It also focuses on **Quantum Communications**, specifically **Quantum Key Distribution (QKD)** over long distances, including satellite-based secure communications.
 
 
 
• **Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC):**
 
 
• **PQC** refers to mathematical **algorithms** that are thought to be secure against a cryptanalytic attack by a **quantum computer**.
 
• The **QSIP** chip integrates these **PQC** standards to ensure that data remains protected even as quantum computing power scales globally.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Applications:**
 
 
• The chip is designed for use in **critical infrastructure** such as **power grids**, **banking systems**, and **strategic defense networks**.
 
• It facilitates **Quantum Random Number Generation (QRNG)**, which provides a higher level of entropy compared to classical pseudo-random generators, making encryption keys nearly impossible to predict.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Semiconductor Mission connection:** The production of the **QSIP** chip is part of the broader **India Semiconductor Mission (ISM)**, which seeks to build a vibrant semiconductor and display ecosystem in the country.
 
• **Global Standing:** With the launch of **QSIP**, India joins an elite group of nations—including the **USA**, **China**, and **France**—that possess high-end **quantum-secure hardware** technology.
 
• **Cybersecurity Landscape:** As quantum computers can solve complex mathematical problems in seconds that would take classical computers **thousands of years**, the **QSIP** serves as a vital shield against "harvest now, decrypt later" strategies used by cyber-adversaries.
 
• **Collaborative Effort:** The design of the chip involved collaboration between the **Department of Science and Technology (DST)**, premier institutes like **IITs**, and **defense research laboratories**.
